questions.stem: Which type of radiation is the most strongly ionising?
questions.explanation: Alpha radiation is the most strongly ionising because alpha particles are relatively large and heavy (2 protons + 2 neutrons) with a charge of +2. They interact strongly with nearby atoms, knocking electrons off them. However, this also means they lose energy quickly and have the shortest range.

questions.stem: What is the main property of radioactive decay that means we cannot predict exactly when a particular nucleus will decay?
questions.explanation: Radioactive decay is random, meaning we cannot predict when any particular nucleus will decay. We can only describe the probability of decay. The term 'spontaneous' means it happens without an external trigger, which is a separate (also important) property of radioactive decay.
